business_information.description: A United States title-insurance and settlement-services business serving residential purchase, refinance, home-equity, construction, and selected commercial real-estate transactions. Services include title-order intake, title search and examination, curative processing, underwriting, commitments, owner and lender policies, endorsements, closing, settlement, escrow, recording, property information, independent-agent oversight, premium remittance, and claims administration. Business is produced through direct branches, centralized lender channels, and independent title agents. The model must preserve evidence, provenance, effective-dated ownership interests, lifecycle history, and the legal and operational distinctions among searches, examinations, findings, requirements, exceptions, commitments, policies, settlement statements, and escrow ledgers.

business_context.vibe_modeling_instructions: Generate the MVM first and use it as the approved foundation for the ECM. Keep title_order, title_search, title_examination, title_finding, title_requirement, policy_exception, title_commitment, and title_policy as distinct entities. Keep settlement_statement and escrow_ledger as distinct entities. Model property, parcel, and legal_description separately. Model ownership as effective-dated ownership_interest records supported by evidence rather than a single current-owner attribute. Model party roles contextually so one party can hold multiple simultaneous roles. Preserve material lifecycle transitions, revisions, and prior classifications. Separate document execution_date, effective_date, submission_date, acceptance_date, and recording_date. Require evidence and provenance relationships for material title findings and underwriting decisions. Keep owner and lender policies as separate policy records and policy types. Every title policy must reference an originating title order. Treat bank account, wire instruction, identity document, signature, tax identifier, and non-public personal information as restricted. The MVM must cover core direct title and settlement workflows plus the minimum agency and claims concepts needed for end-to-end analysis. Expand detailed agency authority, audit, remittance, advanced claim financials, commercial transactions, regulatory reporting, fraud controls, retention, and legal hold primarily in the ECM. Use the synthetic Google Drive knowledge source IDs in documentation and requirement traceability where possible.
